cases.sentence: — А помнишь ты, — сказала Наташа с задумчивою улыбкой, как давно, давно, мы еще совсем маленькие были, дяденька нас позвал в кабинет, еще в ___, а темно было — мы пришли и вдруг там стоит...
cases.explain: «старом доме» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “And do you remember,” Natásha asked with a pensive smile, “how once, long, long ago, when we were quite little, Uncle called us into the study—that was in the old house—and it was dark—we went in and suddenly there stood …”

cases.sentence: — Он серый был, помнишь, и ___ — стоит и смотрит на нас...
cases.explain: «белые зубы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “He was gray, you remember, and had white teeth, and stood and looked at us. …”

cases.sentence: Соня не помнила многого из того, чтò они вспоминали, а и то, чтó она помнила, не возбуждало в ней того ___, которое они испытывали.
cases.explain: «поэтического чувства» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Much that they remembered had slipped from her mind, and what she recalled did not arouse the same poetic feeling as they experienced. She simply enjoyed their pleasure and tried to fit in with it.

cases.sentence: Она приняла участие только в том, когда они вспоминали ___ Сони.
cases.explain: «первый приезд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: She only really took part when they recalled Sónya’s first arrival. She told them how afraid she had been of Nikoláy because he had on a corded jacket and her nurse had told her that she, too, would be sewn up with cords.

cases.sentence: Он снял сукно, и арфа издала ___.
cases.explain: «фальшивый звук» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: In the middle of their talk in the sitting room, Dimmler came in and went up to the harp that stood there in a corner. He took off its cloth covering, and the harp gave out a jarring sound.

cases.sentence: — Эдуард Карлыч, сыграйте пожалуста мой любимый Nocturne мосье Фильда, — сказал голос ___ из гостиной.
cases.explain: «старой графини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Eduárd Karlých, please play my favorite nocturne by Field,” came the old countess’ voice from the drawing room.

cases.sentence: В комнате, особенно на диване, на котором они сидели, было темно, но в ___ падал на пол серебряный свет полного месяца.
cases.explain: «большие окна» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Dimmler began to play; Natásha went on tiptoe noiselessly to the table, took up a candle, carried it out, and returned, seating herself quietly in her former place. It was dark in the room especially where they were sitting on the sofa, but through the big windows the silvery light of the full moon fell on the floor. Dimmler had finished the piece but still sat softly running his fingers over the strings, evidently uncertain whether to stop or to play something else.

cases.sentence: — Да, но трудно нам представить вечность, — сказал Диммлер, который подошел к ___ с кроткою презрительною улыбкой, но теперь говорил так же тихо и серьезно, как и они.
cases.explain: «молодым людям» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Yes, but it is hard for us to imagine eternity,” remarked Dimmler, who had joined the young folk with a mildly condescending smile but now spoke as quietly and seriously as they.

cases.sentence: — Нынче будет, завтра будет, всегда будет и вчера было и ___ было...
cases.explain: «третьего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why is it hard to imagine eternity?” said Natásha. “It is now today, and it will be tomorrow, and always; and there was yesterday, and the day before. …”

cases.sentence: Соня, слушая, думала о том, какая ___ была между ей и ее другом и как невозможно было ей хоть на сколько-нибудь быть столь обворожительною, как ее кузина.
cases.explain: «громадная разница» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: She had said she did not want to sing, but it was long since she had sung, and long before she again sang, as she did that evening. The count, from his study where he was talking to Mítenka, heard her and, like a schoolboy in a hurry to run out to play, blundered in his talk while giving orders to the steward, and at last stopped, while Mítenka stood in front of him also listening and smiling. Nikoláy did not take his eyes off his sister and drew breath in time with her. Sónya, as she listened, thought of the immense difference there was between herself and her friend, and how impossible it was for her to be anything like as bewitching as her cousin. The old countess sat with a blissful yet sad smile and with tears in her eyes, occasionally shaking her head. She thought of Natásha and of her own youth, and of how there was something unnatural and dreadful in this impending marriage of Natásha and Prince Andréy.

cases.sentence: ___ сидела с счастливо-грустною улыбкой и слезами на глазах, изредка покачивая головой.
cases.explain: «Старая графиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
